Writing the rewrite of `codevetter.com/download` surfaced three claims on the live page that do not currently hold. Filing together because they share one likely root cause: the cutover to the native SwiftUI release pipeline.

## 1. The six newest releases ship no downloadable build

`v1.12.0` through `v1.13.2` — six releases cut between 2026-09-04 23:11Z and 2026-09-05 11:10Z — all have **zero release assets**.

The newest release carrying a DMG is **v1.11.1 (2026-09-03)**. Every release from `v1.5.3` onward carries four assets, so this is a regression rather than intent.

The `/download` page's "Latest release →" link therefore sends visitors to a release with nothing to download.

`PROJECT_STATUS.md:43` describes `auto-release.yml` cutting a `v<version>` tag on `Shared.xcconfig` version bumps while `release.yml` signs, notarizes, qualifies and uploads. That split is consistent with tags being cut while the upload job does not complete.

## 2. The documented filename pattern matches no published asset

`/download` states the artifact is `CodeVetter-<version>-arm64.dmg`.

Every published asset is `CodeVetter_<version>_aarch64.dmg` — underscores, and `aarch64` rather than `arm64`. Anyone scripting against the documented name gets nothing.

## 3. The Sparkle auto-update claim is contradicted by the repo's own evidence

`/download` states installed copies "update through the in-app Sparkle appcast".

- `https://codevetter.com/appcast.xml` → **404**
- `evidence/verification/native-release-readiness-2026-09-02.md:28` — "no production HTTPS Sparkle appcast is configured"
- `crates/codevetter-core/src/capabilities.rs:298` — "Sparkle is locally packaged but remains disabled until production signing, appcast, EdDSA, and installed-upgrade gates pass"
- `crates/codevetter-core/src/capabilities.rs:666` — "Sparkle remains inactive unless a production HTTPS appcast and EdDSA public key are present"

On the evidence available, auto-update is not live. I could not disprove that it was enabled in the days since 2026-09-02 — there is no appcast at the conventional URL and nothing in the repo points at another one. Someone with the deploy view should confirm.

This is the most expensive of the three to leave standing: a download page asserting an update mechanism that the product's own verification evidence says is disabled sits badly against "Review suggests. Evidence decides."

## Suggested fixes

- Make `release.yml` fail loudly when a tag is cut without assets uploaded, so this cannot regress silently again.
- Correct the filename pattern on `/download`, or template it from the release feed.
- Either enable the production appcast or change the page to say updates are manual for now.
- Template the version string on `/download` rather than hardcoding — six releases landed in under 13 hours.

---

## What blocks

`native-production-qualification.yml` fails at **Qualify isolated upgrade, relaunch, custom rubric, data, and rollback**, which is the last gate before release assets upload. No release has ever published assets because of it.

```
Command failed: .../codevetter-native-upgrade/installation/CodeVetter.app/Contents/MacOS/codevetter \
  rubrics --id hosted-migration-proof --name Hosted migration proof ... --json
codevetter: unknown command `rubrics`
```

Observed on run [33962630311](https://github.com/Codevetter/codevetter/actions/runs/33962630311) for `v1.13.2`.

## Why

The workflow pins the incumbent to the last Tauri release:

```yaml
gh release download v1.11.0 --pattern 'CodeVetter_aarch64.app.tar.gz'
```

`v1.11.0` is the newest tag carrying assets, so it is the only usable incumbent. Its bundled CLI predates the `rubrics` command, but the proof uses `rubrics` to create the durable record whose survival across upgrade and rollback is the thing being proven. The incumbent can never seed that data, so the gate cannot pass as written.

## Decisions needed

This is a product decision about what the migration guarantee asserts, not a mechanical fix:

1. Seed the durable record with a command the `v1.11.0` CLI does have, and assert survival of that instead.
2. Publish assets for a newer incumbent first, then pin to it.
3. Narrow the proof to data written by the candidate itself, accepting that cross-shell migration from Tauri is no longer exercised.

## Context

`PROJECT_STATUS.md` lists the exact-archive installed-upgrade proof as pending under #249 tasks 6-8, but #249 is closed, so this was untracked.

Everything before this gate now passes: Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, and Sparkle appcast generation and cryptographic inspection.

issues.body:
## Why

Pace currently consumes third-party MCP servers, but it does not expose its own local Mac capabilities to Codex. That leaves Pace isolated from the agent doing the broader work and makes Codex recreate context or use generic APIs instead of asking the app that already owns local screen understanding, memory, approvals, and the iPad companion.

The goal is not to turn Pace into another generic connector catalog or another reasoning layer. The goal is to make Pace the local, physical capability layer for Codex while preserving Pace's on-device privacy boundary and existing user-approval system.

## What

### In scope for V1

- Add an opt-in, loopback-only Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint hosted by the running Pace Mac app.
- Require an explicit in-app connection approval before an MCP session becomes usable. The session is ephemeral, single-client, and invalidated when Pace quits or MCP access is disabled.
- Expose a deliberately small set of Pace-only tools:
  - `pace_get_status`: report Pace readiness, permission state, current interaction state, and iPad companion connection state.
  - `pace_observe_screen`: return semantic current-screen context from Pace's existing AX-first, OCR-enriched, VLM-fallback pipeline. Do not return a raw screenshot by default.
  - `pace_search_memory`: search Pace's existing local unified memory with its current sensitive-topic filtering.
  - `pace_execute_action`: execute a typed action through the existing tool registry, preflight, approval, audit, and action executor. Codex does not send arbitrary shell commands and does not bypass Pace approval.
  - `pace_notify_companion`: display and optionally speak a bounded message through Pace's existing restrained proactive pipeline and connected iPad.
- Return structured, bounded results that Codex can reason about without sending them through Pace's planner.
- Publish concise MCP server instructions describing when Codex should use Pace and when it should use a direct API instead.
- Add a project-scoped example configuration and a setup surface in Pace that shows the exact local Codex command/config without writing to Codex configuration automatically.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Generic GitHub, Gmail, calendar, weather, web-fetch, filesystem, or SaaS API wrappers when Codex can use the direct API or an existing MCP server.
- A natural-language `ask_pace` tool that sends Codex requests back through Pace's planner; that creates duplicate reasoning and a recursion risk when Codex is the caller.
- Arbitrary shell execution.
- Bypassing macOS TCC, Pace's preflight checks, or Pace's mutation approvals.
- Cloud relay, remote internet access, multi-user access, or multiple simultaneous MCP clients.
- Continuous screen capture, raw screen streaming, camera streaming, or automatic memory export.
- Making the iPad a second intelligence or MCP host.

## Design

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Codex[Codex local client] -->|Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1| MCP[Pace MCP adapter]
    MCP --> Session[Ephemeral in-app session approval]
    Session --> Context[AX + OCR + VLM screen context]
    Session --> Memory[Unified local memory retriever]
    Session --> Actions[Typed Pace action facade]
    Session --> Companion[Mac + iPad companion output]
    Actions --> Preflight[Tool registry + preflight]
    Preflight --> Approval[Pace approval UI]
    Approval --> Executor[Existing action executor + audit]
```

### Transport and lifecycle

- Bind a fixed documented port on `127.0.0.1` only; never advertise this endpoint over Bonjour or bind to the LAN interface.
- Keep MCP disabled by default. Enabling it starts the listener and shows a persistent status/disable control in Settings.
- On `initialize`, Pace shows which local client is requesting access. Approval creates one in-memory MCP session ID. Reject concurrent clients and invalidate the session on app quit, disable, or explicit disconnect.
- Fail loud when the port is occupied or Pace lacks a required permission. Do not silently fall back to another interface or cloud path.
- Implement only the MCP methods needed for Codex V1: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`, with protocol/version and JSON-RPC error coverage.
- Use tool annotations and Codex setup guidance so read-only tools are distinguishable from mutating tools. Pace's own approval gate remains authoritative for mutations regardless of Codex configuration.

### Tool behavior

- `pace_get_status` is fast and does not start the planner, VLM, or microphone.
- `pace_observe_screen` respects the existing Read My Screen preference and visible activity indicators. It uses AX first, OCR enrichment second, and VLM only when needed. Results are semantic and size-bounded.
- `pace_search_memory` reuses `PaceMemoryRetriever`, honors exclusions and sensitive-topic preferences, and returns a typed result rather than the planner-formatted context block.
- `pace_execute_action` accepts only typed registry-backed actions. It performs `PaceToolPreflight`, invokes the existing approval surface when required, executes through `PaceActionExecutor`, and returns the resulting observations. No planner hop is involved.
- `pace_notify_companion` reuses the existing restraint and proactive queue. It must not speak during active calls, focus suppression, quiet mode, or a conflicting conversation.

### Privacy and audit

- MCP calls remain on-device and are recorded in the existing local API/audit log with tool name, duration, outcome, and output size; never record raw screen images, memory payloads, or session identifiers.
- The Pace UI must make MCP connected/active state visible and provide one-click disconnect.
- Screen and memory tools must return a clear disabled/permission result rather than changing privacy preferences.
- Requested raw screenshots, camera frames, and unrestricted memory export remain unavailable in V1.

## Specs

### Connection and session

- **Given** MCP access is disabled, **when** a local client connects, **then** no Pace tool or context is exposed.
- **Given** MCP access is enabled, **when** Codex initializes a session, **then** Pace requires explicit local approval before returning a usable session.
- **Given** an approved session, **when** Pace quits, MCP is disabled, or the user disconnects it, **then** the session becomes unusable immediately.
- **Given** an active session, **when** a second client initializes, **then** Pace rejects it without replacing the approved client.
- **Given** the configured port is occupied, **when** MCP starts, **then** Pace shows an actionable local error and does not bind another interface.

### Read-only tools

- **Given** Pace is running, **when** Codex calls `pace_get_status`, **then** it receives bounded structured state without starting any model.
- **Given** Read My Screen is enabled and permission is granted, **when** Codex calls `pace_observe_screen`, **then** it receives semantic AX/OCR/VLM-fallback context and no raw image bytes.
- **Given** Read My Screen is disabled or permission is missing, **when** the screen tool is called, **then** it returns a typed disabled/permission result and does not alter settings.
- **Given** a memory query, **when** Codex calls `pace_search_memory`, **then** results come from the existing local memory index and obey current sensitive-topic filtering.

### Actions and companion

- **Given** a valid registry-backed action that does not require approval, **when** Codex calls `pace_execute_action`, **then** Pace performs normal preflight, execution, observation, and audit behavior.
- **Given** a mutation or blocked preflight, **when** Codex calls `pace_execute_action`, **then** Pace shows its existing approval UI and executes only after Allow Once.
- **Given** an unknown tool, malformed arguments, or arbitrary shell request, **when** Codex calls the action tool, **then** Pace rejects it before execution.
- **Given** companion speech is currently restrained, **when** Codex calls `pace_notify_companion`, **then** the message queues or remains silent according to the existing restraint policy.

### End-to-end acceptance

- From a real local Codex session, `pace_get_status`, `pace_observe_screen`, and `pace_search_memory` return useful results from the running Pace app.
- From the same session, a safe typed action completes and a mutation cannot complete without Pace approval.
- A companion message visibly reaches the Mac surface and, when connected, the iPad.
- Restarting Pace invalidates the old MCP session; reconnecting requires a fresh in-app approval and does not require editing configuration.
- The full Pace unit suite, MCP protocol integration tests, docs validation, and a real-hardware smoke pass are green.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add MCP protocol DTOs, JSON-RPC validation, bounded response/error types, and unit tests.
- [ ] Add the loopback-only listener, fixed-port failure handling, ephemeral single-client session approval, disconnect, and lifecycle tests.
- [ ] Add `pace_get_status` without model startup.
- [ ] Extract a typed semantic observation result from `PaceScreenContextService` and add `pace_observe_screen` with privacy/permission tests.
- [ ] Add a typed read-only search facade over `PaceMemoryRetriever` and cover sensitive-topic filtering.
- [ ] Add a typed action decoder over `PaceToolRegistry`, route through preflight/approval/executor, and add rejection/approval tests.
- [ ] Route `pace_notify_companion` through the existing restraint/proactive pipeline and companion server.
- [ ] Add MCP connected/active/error controls and one-click disconnect to Pace Settings.
- [ ] Add server instructions and a project-scoped Codex configuration example, aligned with current Codex Streamable HTTP support.
- [ ] Update architecture, key-files, capability, privacy, and project-status docs only as implementation becomes true.
- [ ] Run focused protocol/tool tests, `bash scripts/test-pace.sh`, `bash scripts/validate-docs.sh`, and a real local Codex-to-Pace smoke test.
- [ ] Walk the real-hardware release smoke checklist before any release.

issues.body:
## Goal

Add a fully on-device **Spatial Teach Mode** that lets a user point or paint over part of the Mac UI, speak a request such as “move this there” or “teach this workflow,” and gives Pace an exact, window-bound context packet. When the user demonstrates repeated work, compile that trace into an evidence-rich deterministic flow that replays without a model on the healthy path and halts when the target or result cannot be proven.

This combines four useful patterns while preserving Pace's native Swift runtime, privacy moat, approval model, and RAM discipline:

| Source | Pattern to adapt for Pace |
| --- | --- |
| [Supamaus Lite](https://lite.supamaus.com/) | A spatial context packet containing screenshot/crop, gesture trail or regions, spoken/typed instruction, and the window's text; short-lived capture sessions across displays. |
| [TipTour macOS](https://github.com/milind-soni/tiptour-macos) | Listen-only freeform highlight chord; bind the trail to window ID/PID/bundle/title, intersected AX element, and selected text; “Autopilot” vs “Tour Guide” presentation; local CoreML + Vision grounding shape. |
| [CUA Driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/main/libs/cua-driver) | Exact `(pid, window_id)` targeting with ambiguity refusal; window-scoped capture; separate typed action facts from caller-defined postcondition verification; short lifecycle sessions and trajectories. |
| [OpenAdapt Flow](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-flow) | Treat a demonstration as source, compile it into redundant target evidence + pre/postconditions, replay deterministically, and halt/teach/promote a reviewed repair instead of guessing. |

## Why this belongs in Pace

Pace already owns the hard native substrate: push-to-talk, ScreenCaptureKit, AX/OCR/VLM context, cursor/annotation overlays, approval/audit/undo, plan-act-observe, recorded flows, deterministic Programs, and planner-grounded skills.

The missing seam is between “the user means **this**” and “Pace can safely reuse that demonstration later”:

- Teach-by-demonstration is already listed as deferred in [the teachable-skills PRD](https://github.com/HeyPace/pace/blob/main/docs/product/prds/teachable-skills.md).
- `PaceRecordedStep.axPress` persists only a role path and label in [PaceFlowReplay.swift](https://github.com/HeyPace/pace/blob/main/leanring-buddy/PaceFlowReplay.swift).
- The flow replayer resolves an AX target, but its production action sink cannot carry the live AX element and re-resolves at the current cursor position in [PaceFlowReplayer.swift](https://github.com/HeyPace/pace/blob/main/leanring-buddy/PaceFlowReplayer.swift). Spatial teaching must close that identity/dispatch gap before adding broader replay.

## Proposed v1

### 1. Short-lived spatial context packet

Introduce a pure versioned value such as `PaceSpatialContextPacket` containing only the evidence available for the current interaction:

- stable packet/session ID and timestamp;
- display ID and coordinate-space metadata;
- sampled/capped gesture polyline, bounding region, direction, and optional multiple named regions (`this`, `there`);
- exact hovered window identity: PID, CGWindowID, bundle identifier, app name, title, and frame;
- intersected/focused AX element evidence: identifier, role/subrole, label/title/description/value shape, frame, and ancestor fingerprint;
- selected-text evidence when available, excluding secure fields;
- tightly cropped screenshot evidence plus local Vision OCR/AX window text;
- the on-device speech transcript or typed instruction;
- explicit provenance and privacy flags for every field.

The packet is bounded-memory and interaction-scoped by default. Pace overlays must be excluded from capture. Do not persist a full-window screenshot merely because a packet was created.

### 2. Spatial highlight interaction

- Add a configurable hold-to-highlight chord (provisional default: Control+Shift) using a listen-only event tap.
- Render the sampled trail and named endpoints/regions in Pace's existing non-activating overlay.
- On release, bind the trail to the exact window and strongest available AX/text evidence.
- Support at minimum:
  - “what is this?”
  - “click this”
  - “change this text”
  - “move this there”
  - “teach/record this workflow”
- Keep the normal approval path authoritative. A gesture narrows intent; it does not grant action authority.

### 3. Evidence-rich `PaceRecordedFlow` v2

Migrate v1 flows without breaking their current JSON representation. New steps should be able to retain:

- action and typed arguments/parameter placeholders;
- exact app/window identity;
- structural AX locator and ancestor evidence;
- optional local crop, OCR label, nearby landmarks, and recorded coordinate as fallback evidence;
- risk class;
- bounded precondition and postcondition;
- whether a model fallback is allowed;
- provenance, schema version, and integrity digest.

Compilation should remove incidental input, group typing, suppress secrets, infer only conservative literal parameters, and refuse partial/ambiguous output. Healthy replay makes no planner/VLM call.

### 4. Fail-closed resolution and execution contract

Use a Pace-native ladder:

1. exact AX identifier/handle inside the exact recorded PID + window;
2. unique AX role/name/ancestor match inside that window;
3. local crop/template + OCR/landmark evidence;
4. optional on-device VLM grounding when the step policy allows it;
5. halt and ask the user to re-teach.

Ambiguity is a refusal, not permission to fall through to a weaker rung. Carry the resolved live AX element or an opaque execution handle through dispatch; never substitute the user's current cursor position.

Separate:

- **Action fact:** confirmed / partial / unverifiable / suspected-noop / refused, plus route and evidence.
- **Postcondition:** satisfied / unsatisfied / unknown.

Only `satisfied` advances a dependent consequential step. Preserve the completed prefix and leave the suffix unattempted after failure.

### 5. Repair and guide surfaces

- On drift, show what Pace expected, what it found, and the exact halted step.
- Let the user point at the corrected target and produce a reviewable repair candidate.
- Do not silently mutate the active flow. Promote only after a deterministic regression replay.
- Reuse the cursor overlay for a “Guide me” mode that points/narrates one step at a time without acting. This is presentation over the same compiled flow, not a separate workflow format.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An OpenSpec proposal defines the packet, flow-v2 schema, migration, privacy retention, resolver ladder, typed outcomes, and failure states before implementation.
- [ ] A user can hold the highlight chord, draw a visible freeform trail, release it, and receive a packet bound to the correct display and exact app/window.
- [ ] `this` and `there` can be represented as distinct regions in one bounded interaction.
- [ ] AX element/text selection evidence is preferred; secure text is never captured or serialized.
- [ ] Full screenshots remain ephemeral; persisted flows retain only the minimum approved crops/evidence needed for deterministic replay.
- [ ] Existing v1 flows load and replay without behavior drift.
- [ ] A v2 replay performs the resolved AX action on the resolved target rather than the current physical cursor.
- [ ] Multiple eligible windows or elements return a typed ambiguity refusal before input.
- [ ] Every mutating step returns an action fact; every dependent step with a required result waits for a separate typed postcondition.
- [ ] Theme change, moved control, and safe label drift succeed through stronger retained evidence where possible.
- [ ] Wrong app/window, duplicate labels without independent identity, occlusion, surprise modal, missing permission, and unverifiable postcondition halt before later dependent actions.
- [ ] Failed drift creates a reviewable repair candidate; the active flow is unchanged until promotion.
- [ ] Guide mode can point/narrate compiled steps without performing them.
- [ ] Spatial capture, compilation, replay, and repair stay on-device and produce no network egress.
- [ ] Focused unit/fixture tests run through `bash scripts/test-pace.sh <suite>`; do not invoke terminal `xcodebuild`.

## Evaluation matrix

Measure at least:

- correct completion;
- silent incorrect completion;
- safe halt;
- unnecessary halt;
- resolution rung used;
- action-to-evidence latency;
- planner/VLM calls on healthy replay;
- peak memory and retained artifact size.

Fixtures should cover two windows from one PID, two same-label siblings, moved/renamed controls, theme drift, AX-sparse/canvas UI, stale screenshots, display scaling, multi-monitor coordinates, secure fields, user cancellation, and surprise dialogs.

## Privacy, licensing, and release boundaries

- No cloud LLM/STT/VLM path may be introduced. TipTour's Gemini/Worker path is explicitly not applicable to Pace.
- Supamaus Lite is a commercial closed product: borrow the interaction concept only, not implementation or assets.
- CUA and TipTour use/private-reference undocumented SkyLight and AX SPI for background input. Do **not** ship private-API background control in v1. Any later experiment must be isolated behind a separate release/legal/TCC evaluation and may not silently replace Pace's public AX/CGEvent path.
- Do not turn Pace into an unauthenticated local screen-serving MCP/HTTP server. Any future external context export requires a separate threat model, explicit per-client consent, visible off-device indication when relevant, and audit logging.
- TipTour's bundled `UIElementDetector.mlpackage` identifies itself as an Ultralytics YOLO11m artifact under AGPL-3.0 and does not establish training-data provenance. Do **not** copy its model or weights. A Pace detector must use a verified permissive model/data chain or be trained in-house and benchmarked against the existing AX + OCR + set-of-mark/VLM path.
- OpenAdapt-authored engine code and CUA/TipTour source are MIT, but copied substantial code requires retained attribution. OpenAdapt's isolated AGPL benchmark files are outside its MIT package boundary.
- Do not add a Python/Rust daemon or new production dependency for v1. Port the narrow contracts into Pace's existing native Swift process.

## Out of scope for v1

- Cross-platform or VM/sandbox infrastructure.
- Background/no-focus input through private macOS APIs.
- An external MCP context server for Codex/Claude.
- Cloud repair or hosted workflow storage.
- Full autonomous generalization from multiple demonstrations.
- Persisting raw screen history.

- Define a complete Clarity capability policy for each canonically wired public surface.
- Treat recordings, heatmaps, automatic Smart Events, Copilot insights, and AI Visibility as the default desired baseline for every eligible public surface.
- Define product-specific custom events and funnels from real routes and user actions.
- Track provider-side configuration and verification separately from source wiring and deployment.
- Report capability coverage inside the existing Site Health project evidence surface and fleet collector.
- Use focused MCP session-recording investigation without persisting raw recordings or visitor identifiers.

Out of scope:

- Inventing browser surfaces for native-only, local-only, retired, archived, or resource-only products.
- Silently overriding an explicit product promise of no analytics or telemetry.
- Capturing passwords, payment values, private inboxes, private documents, health data, or user-provided model inputs.
- Storing API tokens, raw recordings, heatmap payloads, URLs containing sensitive values, or visitor identifiers in Site Health.
- Deploying products, generating tokens, or weakening legally required consent without separate authorization.

## Design

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[Canonical Clarity receipt] --> P[Per-product capability policy]
  P --> S[Source instrumentation]
  P --> U[Provider settings audit]
  S --> C[Clarity capture]
  U --> C
  C --> E[Data Export aggregates]
  C --> M[Focused MCP investigation]
  E --> H[Site Health evidence]
  M --> H
```

The canonical SaaS Maker Clarity receipt remains the identity and source-wiring authority. Site Health projects a capability contract and provider verification state; it never treats a desired setting as observed. Passive Clarity features default on for wired public surfaces. Custom events and funnels remain product-specific. Provider-side state, source state, deployment state, and observed data are separate gates.

## Specs

### Requirement: Full capability accounting

Site Health SHALL report every relevant Clarity capability for every canonical identity as enabled, desired, not applicable, blocked, or unverified.

#### Scenario: A wired public product has no provider audit

- **WHEN** the canonical receipt proves source wiring but no signed-in settings receipt exists
- **THEN** passive features are reported as desired and provider-unverified
- **AND** Site Health does not claim they are enabled.

### Requirement: Product-specific behavior measurement

Every eligible product SHOULD define meaningful conversion events and at least one funnel when its real user journey contains two or more observable steps.

#### Scenario: A marketing-only landing has one outbound action

- **WHEN** no multi-step on-site journey exists
- **THEN** the product uses an explicit CTA event
- **AND** records the funnel as not applicable rather than inventing steps.

### Requirement: Privacy and product boundaries

Full Clarity adoption SHALL preserve explicit no-telemetry promises and hard sensitive-data exclusions.

#### Scenario: A private or sensitive route exists beside a public surface

- **WHEN** the public surface is instrumented
- **THEN** private routes remain excluded or strictly masked
- **AND** Site Health records that boundary.

### Requirement: Honest provider verification

Provider settings SHALL be changed only through authenticated Clarity controls and verified after mutation.

#### Scenario: Browser control is unavailable

- **WHEN** the authenticated Clarity workspace cannot be controlled
- **THEN** source and policy work continues
- **AND** provider settings remain explicitly blocked rather than inferred.

### Requirement: Bounded internal evidence

Site Health SHALL retain only normalized aggregate metrics and capability receipts.

#### Scenario: An operator investigates session recordings through MCP

- **WHEN** a focused read-only investigation runs
- **THEN** raw playback data and visitor identifiers are not persisted
- **AND** only a bounded conclusion may be recorded.

- [x] 3. Render aggregate Clarity evidence in existing project details.
- [x] 4. Add a canonical per-project Clarity capability policy and validator.
- [x] 5. Add Site Health capability coverage projections and focused tests.

issues.body:
## Why

Fleet has recurring web extraction and public-media acquisition work, but the reusable skill catalog does not currently encode how to choose safe, bounded tooling or produce receipts. SEO research also needs provider-backed keyword and competitor data without duplicating Fleet's existing technical SEO audit or making a paid provider mandatory.

Repository evidence already shows `yt-dlp` in active LoopTV and High Signal workflows. Scrapling has a maintained agent-facing extraction surface. OpenSEO publishes useful research workflows, while Maxun, Crawl4AI, and Treg would overlap existing capabilities or introduce platform, credential, cost, or routing concerns.

## What

In scope:

- Add a Fleet-owned `web-extraction` skill using Scrapling as an optional structured-crawl backend.
- Add a Fleet-owned `media-acquisition` skill using the already-installed `yt-dlp`; reserve Instaloader as a conditional future backend rather than adding it now.
- Add a Fleet-owned `seo-research` skill for keyword, competitor, backlink-prospect, and local-search research, with OpenSEO as an optional provider-backed evidence source.
- Route provider-optional SEO research from the existing `site-health` parent.
- Expose the three skills through Fleet's selected runtime catalog.
- Add execution profiles, Codex UI metadata, validation coverage, and bounded receipt contracts.

Out of scope:

- Installing Scrapling, browsers, Instaloader, OpenSEO, MCP servers, or production dependencies.
- Reading or storing cookies, credentials, environment files, provider response bodies, or private provider data.
- Bypassing access controls, scraping authenticated pages, downloading media without rights, or making paid provider calls without explicit user intent.
- Adding Maxun, Crawl4AI, or Treg to the default Fleet skill surface.
- Replacing Fleet's existing `seo-audit`, Site Health collectors, browser tools, or repository-local product pipelines.

## Design

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Operator request] --> R{Capability router}
  R --> W[web-extraction]
  R --> M[media-acquisition]
  R --> S[seo-research]
  W --> B[Built-in browser or Scrapling if available]
  M --> Y[yt-dlp public metadata and media]
  S --> F[First-party and cached evidence]
  S --> O[Optional OpenSEO MCP]
  W --> E[Bounded receipt]
  M --> E
  F --> E
  O --> E
```

Each skill owns decision guidance and evidence semantics, not a copied upstream manual. Missing optional tools and provider access are reported as `unavailable`, never silently installed or converted to zero. Existing product-specific scripts remain authoritative where they exist.

## Specs

### Requirement: Safe web extraction

The `web-extraction` skill SHALL start with the least invasive available method and SHALL treat authenticated access, anti-bot evasion, proxy use, and CAPTCHA solving as outside its default workflow.

#### Scenario: Scrapling is unavailable

- **WHEN** a structured crawl would benefit from Scrapling but its executable or package is absent
- **THEN** the skill reports the backend as unavailable
- **AND** does not install it without explicit authorization.

### Requirement: Reproducible public-media acquisition

The `media-acquisition` skill SHALL default to metadata inspection before downloads and SHALL preserve source URL, selected format, output location, and command outcome in its receipt.

#### Scenario: A user requests YouTube catalog metadata

- **WHEN** `yt-dlp` is available and the target is public
- **THEN** the skill uses metadata-only and flat-playlist modes where sufficient
- **AND** avoids downloading media bytes unnecessarily.

### Requirement: Provider-optional SEO research

The `seo-research` skill SHALL distinguish measured, cached, unavailable, and inferred evidence and SHALL not require OpenSEO for credential-free research.

#### Scenario: OpenSEO is not connected

- **WHEN** keyword volume, difficulty, backlink, or local SERP metrics require OpenSEO and its MCP is unavailable
- **THEN** the skill marks those fields unavailable with the exact reason
- **AND** continues with first-party, live-page, Search Console, or cached evidence that is actually available.

### Requirement: Non-overlapping routing

The new skills SHALL NOT replace technical SEO audit, browser interaction, or product-specific ingestion pipelines.

#### Scenario: The user asks for title, canonical, sitemap, or structured-data checks

- **WHEN** the request is technical on-page SEO rather than market research
- **THEN** `site-health` routes to the existing `seo-audit` skill instead of `seo-research`.

### Requirement: Selected runtime exposure

All three skills SHALL be discoverable from Fleet-selected agent runtimes and carry valid execution profiles and interface metadata.

#### Scenario: Tooling validation runs

- **WHEN** the capability catalog and skill validators execute
- **THEN** all new skills are counted, linked, and pass the repository contracts.

## Tasks

- [x] 1. Add the three skill packages with bounded workflows and receipts.
- [x] 2. Route SEO research from `site-health` and expose all three skills.
- [x] 3. Update catalog expectations and durable project status.
- [x] 4. Run skill, tooling, catalog, and targeted behavioral validation.

issues.body:
## Why

The 10:00 IST report currently runs before the full daily ingest and publish sequence, so it can represent yesterday rather than the current Indian business day. Fresh Digg attention can remain only an overlay until the next batch. Hostname-level corroboration can over-count syndication, publishability checks differ by surface, and signal records do not cleanly separate observed facts from business interpretation.

The operator needs one current-day brief whose material evidence is fresh, whose Digg discoveries enter primary-source verification quickly, and whose publication semantics are identical everywhere.

## What

In scope:

- Move the daily sequence to ingest 08:00 IST, publish 09:00, validate 09:30, deliver 10:00.
- Validate current IST edition date and freshness of material evidence.
- Create threshold-triggered Digg verification work from original source URLs without treating Digg as evidence.
- Normalize claim identity and originating evidence so syndication does not become independent corroboration.
- Create one mandatory publishability evaluator shared by signal APIs, Daily Brief composition, and auto-publish.
- Store observed event, direct entity impact, supply-chain impact, business inference, inference strength, and inference-specific evidence separately.
- Add metrics needed to measure Digg verification latency and publication-quality failures.

Out of scope:

- Scraping Digg story pages or private endpoints.
- Treating Digg summaries as evidence.
- Adding a second equity-price source.
- Rewriting published signal markdown.
- Production migration or deployment without a separate explicit release request.

## Design

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[08:00 IST ingest] --> B[Candidates and claim tuples]
  D[Digg 30 minute poll] --> E{Threshold crossed}
  E -->|yes| F[Original source verification]
  F --> B
  B --> G[Shared publishability evaluator]
  G --> H[09:00 publish]
  H --> I[09:30 IST validation]
  I --> J[10:00 IST delivery]
  G --> K[Signals API and daily dump]
  G --> L[Daily Brief]
```

Schedule times are expressed in UTC in GitHub Actions: 02:30 ingest, 03:30 publish, 04:00 validation, and 04:30 delivery. Validation uses Asia/Kolkata date semantics and rejects a current edition whose newest material evidence is older than two hours.

Digg threshold crossings create idempotent verification requests keyed by cluster and source URL. The verification worker retrieves only underlying original URLs, records first-seen and verified-at timestamps, and routes extracted evidence through existing candidate gates. Digg retains zero evidence/confidence contribution.

Claims use a normalized identity tuple of entity, event, amount, date, and direction plus an originating-evidence identifier. Corroboration requires verified semantic alignment and a distinct evidentiary origin; hostname difference alone is insufficient.

A shared publishability evaluator returns stable violation codes for future dates, prediction-only evidence, unresolved contradictions, impossible direction labels, insufficient independent origins, and same-entity same-event opposite-direction conflicts. Every public surface and auto-publish uses that result.

Signal interpretation fields remain nullable for backward compatibility. Each inference carries its own cited evidence references and a bounded strength value; observed facts stay distinct from inferred business effects.

## Specs

### Requirement: Current IST report sequence
The system SHALL ingest at 08:00 IST, publish at 09:00, validate at 09:30, and deliver at 10:00.

#### Scenario: Daily delivery
- **WHEN** the scheduled report is delivered
- **THEN** its edition date equals the current Asia/Kolkata date
- **AND** its newest material evidence is no more than two hours old

### Requirement: Fast Digg verification
The system SHALL enqueue original-source verification when a Digg cluster crosses configured rank, velocity, or distinct-contributor thresholds.

#### Scenario: Threshold crossing
- **WHEN** a cluster first crosses any materiality threshold
- **THEN** one idempotent verification request is created immediately
- **AND** Digg itself receives no evidence or confidence credit

### Requirement: Origin-aware semantic corroboration
The system SHALL count corroboration only when a source semantically confirms the same normalized claim and traces to a distinct evidentiary origin.

#### Scenario: Syndicated reporting
- **WHEN** multiple hosts repeat one originating report
- **THEN** they count as one evidentiary origin

### Requirement: Mandatory shared publishability
Signals, briefs, public APIs, and auto-publish SHALL use the same publishability result.

#### Scenario: Invalid candidate
- **WHEN** a record is future-dated, prediction-only, contradicted, directionally impossible, or conflicts with an unresolved opposite-direction peer
- **THEN** every publishing surface withholds it using a stable violation code

### Requirement: Observation and inference separation
The system SHALL store observed events separately from direct, supply-chain, and business interpretations.

#### Scenario: Business inference
- **WHEN** an interpretation is attached to an event
- **THEN** it records inference strength and evidence supporting that specific conclusion

## Tasks

- [x] 1. Reschedule ingest, publish, validation, and delivery; add IST date and evidence-freshness validation tests.
- [x] 2. Add idempotent threshold-triggered Digg verification and latency instrumentation.
- [x] 3. Add normalized claim tuples and originating-evidence tracking; require semantic confirmation for corroboration.
- [x] 4. Implement one shared publishability evaluator and wire auto-publish, signal APIs, daily dump, and Daily Brief to it.
- [x] 5. Add structured observation/impact/inference fields, migration, API contracts, and inference-specific citations.
- [x] 6. Run focused tests after each task, then full quality checks and update operational/product documentation.
- [x] 7. Record acceptance receipts and leave migration/deployment pending explicit release authorization.


## September 7 consumer recovery

- Restored and live-tested the installed `get_daily_brief`, `search_signals`, `get_signal`, and `get_track_record` methods in the shared connector; retained the newer daily/evidence tools. CI tests and the production monitor preserve the installed contract.
- Public today/yesterday Brief signals now read the IST publication ledger, including signals published after cached composition. Errors remain unavailable instead of becoming successful empty feeds.
- The daily production freshness validator now verifies Brief, Signals, daily JSON, and installed MCP parity for both public days, plus bounded search/ledger and exact signal lookup.
- Recovery ingest [34094070147](https://github.com/High-Signal-App/high-signal/actions/runs/34094070147) passed: 3,666 events persisted, one draft. Recovery publisher [34096747224](https://github.com/High-Signal-App/high-signal/actions/runs/34096747224) passed freshness and MCP parity; the draft failed the existing editorial structure gate, so September 7 correctly remains without a newly published signal.
- Final live parity: September 7 zero signals; September 6 the same three across surfaces. All four installed methods returned `ok: true`.
- Residual investigation: the original native abort did not recur; all-thread fault diagnostics are enabled, but the responsible library is not identified. The successful recovery also reported four failed generation requests out of ten. Do not equate recovery with proven elimination of those failure modes.

Full receipts: [September 7 incident](https://github.com/High-Signal-App/high-signal/blob/main/docs/operations/2026-09-07-publication-incident.md). This does not close the existing scheduled-chain/Digg latency acceptance work or claim immutable snapshot revisions were implemented.

Fresh Chrome verification on 2026-09-07: opening https://significanthobbies.com/hub lands at https://live.significanthobbies.com/login?returnTo=%2Fhub. No credentials or private Hub data were accessed.

Source evidence:
- services/hub-backend/src/hub.ts sends unauthenticated users to /login?returnTo=%2Fhub.
- Live src/app/login/page.tsx reads callbackUrl only and defaults to /.
- Live safeCallbackUrl permits local paths only; simply replacing the parameter does not establish a safe cross-host Hub return or cookie/session scope.
- The Hub forwards session requests to the Live auth service. Hosted session authority and host handling must be verified, not inferred from a successful login page.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Define and test the full Hub -> login -> authenticated Hub return across the actual hosts, with an explicit allowlist and no open redirects.
2. Preserve existing Live/native authentication identities and user data. Any cookie/binding/production change requires a separate concrete review.
3. Test guest, successful login, expired session, cancelled login and unavailable auth service. Do not redirect indefinitely or silently send a Hub visitor to the Live homepage.
4. Verify two accounts cannot access each other's summaries. Use synthetic test records; do not publish private contents.
5. Retain exact deployed revisions and real browser evidence before qualifying the Hub for sharing.

This is an observed entry-contract defect plus an unqualified cross-host session boundary, not a claim that a hosted session has been repaired. Deployment and auth configuration were not changed.


## Why
The redirect parameter mismatch hides a second defect: Live uses host-only session cookies, while its Worker only delegates apex Hub paths. Returning to apex would lose the Live session; returning to Live /hub currently misses the Hub renderer.

## What
Repair the existing private entry using Live /hub through the existing Hub service binding. Keep Hub rendering/data and Live/native identity ownership unchanged. Exclude deployment, provider setup, cookie-domain changes and private owner data.

## Design
Apex /hub goes to the fixed Live /hub destination. Live /hub delegates only that exact private page through HUB_SERVICE, retaining the request cookie. An anonymous request receives Live /login?callbackUrl=%2Fhub; an authenticated login returns to the same-origin Hub page. Existing returnTo=/hub bookmarks remain accepted only for this exact legacy value. Callback paths reject URL-normalization escape forms. Private page responses and failures use no-store; absent/unavailable auth or Hub binding produces an explicit unavailable response rather than an authentication loop. Root reviewed and authorized this source-backed approach on 2026-09-07.

## Specs
### Requirement: authenticated origin continuity
- WHEN a visitor opens apex /hub, THEN the fixed Live-host private Hub entry SHALL receive the visitor.
- WHEN the visitor signs in, THEN Live SHALL return to /hub and forward the existing session to the Hub authority.
- WHEN auth expires, THEN one sign-in prompt SHALL retain the destination.
### Requirement: fail closed and preserve intent
- WHEN a login is cancelled or rejected, THEN the UI SHALL offer retry and an explicit public directory exit.
- WHEN auth or Hub is unavailable, THEN a no-store unavailable response SHALL terminate the request without redirect loops.
- WHEN untrusted callback/host/path input is supplied, THEN no external redirect or extra Hub delegation SHALL occur.
### Requirement: identity isolation
- WHEN two synthetic accounts request summaries, THEN each SHALL see only its own records through the real session authority; native bearer routes SHALL retain their contract.

## Tasks
- [x] Repair and test exact host/path routing, login intent and unavailable states in both owning repositories.
- [x] Run local synthetic integration with actual session issuance/verification and two-user isolation; retain evidence and limitations.
- [x] Run full owning checks, checked push and verify exact CI.
- [ ] Separately authorize deployment and qualify hosted login/session behavior with exact revisions before shareability.



## Checked source receipts — 2026-09-07

- Hub main `3cd978274e1aed24273b40aec1225fb4e5bfacbf`: [exact CI green](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/significanthobbies/actions/runs/34112613899).
- Live main `b7a47863699ca954cda62a734c67953fddcd8b29`: [exact quality and full browser CI green](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/live/actions/runs/34112604750), [docs green](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/live/actions/runs/34112604719).
- [Local method, screenshots and synthetic account receipts](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/significanthobbies/blob/3cd978274e1aed24273b40aec1225fb4e5bfacbf/docs/hub-login-qualification-2026-09-07.md). Real local Live-issued sessions, two-account Hub isolation, actual database expiry, sign-out revocation, unavailable auth and hydrated retry UI passed.
- Local checks: Hub53 Worker+16 Swift tests; Live586 unit tests/full quality,3 focused browser tests and optimizedbuild. Temporary checkout/databases/TLS files/servers removed; both owning checkouts clean.

No deployment, hosted Google OAuth completion, private owner data access, cookie-domain change or provider mutation occurred. Keep this issue open for the separate hosted qualification task above. Public apex directory remains unchanged; the repaired source uses Live-host /hub as the private authenticated entry.

issues.body:
## Why
The Significant Hobbies Hub joins independently useful Apple-native products, but their visual foundations are drifting. Anchor is currently developing stronger neutral paper/charcoal surfaces, tactile controls, preference groups, responsive layout, and drawn-line motion. Reimplementing those mechanics in every app would create inconsistent quality and repeated bugs; copying Anchor wholesale would erase each product identity.

The product family needs a shared foundation that makes the apps feel related while keeping each app's doodles, accent moments, information architecture, and domain language distinct.

## What

### In scope
- Add a SwiftUI library product named SignificantDesignKit to this repository.
- Define semantic theme roles for canvas, surfaces, text hierarchy, actions, borders, status, spacing, radii, and motion.
- Provide state-free, accessible primitives for tactile buttons, preference groups and rows, responsive content framing, drawn underlines/traces, and Reduce Motion behavior.
- Allow every consumer to supply a product accent, illustration assets, copy, and domain-specific states.
- Use the Hub and Anchor as the first two consumers after the current Anchor visual pass receives owner keep feedback.
- Document an incremental adoption contract for the remaining maintained personal apps.

### Out of scope
- Making every app visually identical.
- Moving product models, storage, navigation, analytics, or local data authority into the Hub.
- Sharing Anchor-specific doodles, interruption colors, habit semantics, or schedule components as generic UI.
- Migrating every product in one unreviewable batch.
- Publishing a package revision or changing consumer pins without explicit release approval.

## Design
SignificantDesignKit is a presentation-only SwiftUI product beside PersonalSyncKit. It owns semantic mechanics and accepts product-provided visual identity. Apps remain independent consumers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  DK[SignificantDesignKit] --> H[Hub]
  DK --> A[Anchor]
  DK --> C[Calorie]
  DK --> K[Kith]
  DK --> S[Setline]
  DK --> SH[Significant Hobbies]
  A --> AI[Anchor doodles and day semantics]
  H --> HI[Hub provenance and product directory]
```

The package SHALL have no dependency on AnchorCore, PersonalSyncKit account state, CloudKit, analytics, or any product store. Theme values SHALL be semantic rather than named after one consumer. Shared motion SHALL honor Reduce Motion. Public components SHALL accept content/action closures rather than embed navigation or persistence.

Deployment impact: none until a new package revision is explicitly committed, pushed, and pinned by consumers. Product adoption remains separate, reviewable changes.

## Specs

### Requirement: Shared family foundation
SignificantDesignKit SHALL expose semantic SwiftUI tokens and components that make Hub products visibly related without requiring identical screens or product accents.

#### Scenario: A product adopts the kit
- **WHEN** an app maps its palette and imports a shared component
- **THEN** the component uses the same spacing, hierarchy, interaction physics, accessibility behavior, and light/dark contract as the family while retaining that product's supplied content and accent

### Requirement: Product boundaries remain strict
The design kit SHALL NOT import product models, storage, sync, or business logic.

#### Scenario: Anchor extracts a preference row
- **WHEN** the row moves into SignificantDesignKit
- **THEN** Anchor continues to own appearance persistence, onboarding actions, behavior-profile counts, Hub status, and all copy

### Requirement: Accessibility is inherited
Shared interactive components SHALL support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, keyboard focus where applicable, 44-point minimum targets, increased contrast, and Reduce Motion.

#### Scenario: Reduce Motion is enabled
- **WHEN** a shared tactile or drawn-line component changes state
- **THEN** meaning and hierarchy remain intact without hover movement, large spatial animation, or looping decoration

### Requirement: Adoption is incremental
Each maintained app SHALL receive a visual review before adopting the shared kit. A consumer SHALL not be migrated solely by mechanical token replacement.

#### Scenario: A product has a distinct visual need
- **WHEN** its operating context conflicts with a default kit treatment
- **THEN** the product supplies an override or keeps a product-owned component rather than weakening the family foundation

## Tasks
- [ ] 1. Inventory current Hub and Apple-product theme systems and record shared roles versus product-owned identity.
- [ ] 2. Add the SignificantDesignKit Swift package product with semantic theme, spacing, radius, motion, and accessibility contracts.
- [ ] 3. Add generic tactile buttons, preference groups/rows, responsive framing, and drawn-line primitives with unit or source-contract tests.
- [ ] 4. Finish and obtain owner keep feedback on the Anchor Settings/core-loop pass before freezing its reusable mechanics.
- [ ] 5. Adopt the kit in Hub and Anchor as separate reviewable changes; verify light/dark, Dynamic Type, keyboard/touch, and Reduce Motion.
- [ ] 6. Document and execute a product-by-product adoption order for the remaining maintained personal apps.
- [ ] 7. Run Hub checks, Swift tests, representative native builds, and responsive visual QA before publishing a package revision.
- [ ] 8. Prepare a release handoff; do not commit, push, publish, or update consumer pins without explicit approval.

## Account PDF affordance repair

Source `1b3456d21cb5d5750a5ef0baec6ada0ed56aed01` removes ineffective font-size/font-family controls for PDFs and labels the supported appearance action as viewer background. It removes the empty Notes tab, keeps explicit AI chat entry, and fixes a reproduced 390px sidebar obstruction that hid the PDF. Desktop retains two panels.

Synthetic authenticated built-browser fixtures verify actual PDF rendering, page navigation, zoom, computed sepia background, absent inert controls, and zero API writes/external calls. Listen receives current-page text through a stubbed speech sink: device audio quality is not qualified. Both guest and account browser journeys pass; independent 390/1440 review finds no blocking issue.

At that revision account page notes were still pending; they are completed by the later receipt below. Hosted Google/D1/R2/provider and real article annotation gates above remain actionable. No live documents, account uploads, credentials, migration or deployment were touched.

The exact pushed revision passed [CI](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/reader/actions/runs/34113990220) and [Docs](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/reader/actions/runs/34113990544). CI includes local IndexedDB, guest PDF and synthetic-account PDF browser checks. This is source/fixture qualification, not hosted or account-annotation completion.

## Account page-note implementation proposal

### Why / What
Complete actual account PDF page-note create/edit/delete/reopen behavior. Existing owner-scoped article PUT supports notes, but its anchor normalizer previously dropped PDF page numbers. Reuse the verified guest page-note interaction and preserve explicit account save/failure feedback. No schema change, migration, AI/provider call, hosted upload or deployment.

### Design
Extract the existing note panel for local/account reuse. Account writes use existing authenticated PUT followed by a canonical read; positive integer PDF page numbers survive normalization. Reader route and PDF queries/drafts are keyed by account plus article, so switching accounts hides prior cached records and draft state. Ownership is enforced by the real handlers and the database user predicate.

### Requirements
- Account notes SHALL retain text and page anchors across save, reload, edit and delete.
- Failed saves SHALL retain the draft and allow explicit retry; success SHALL follow server acknowledgment.
- A second account SHALL neither read nor mutate the first account's document/notes, and switching accounts SHALL hide cached document data and drafts.
- The UI SHALL identify account storage and retain page-note/no-embedded-export wording.

### Local implementation tasks
- [x] Preserve validated PDF page anchors in account persistence.
- [x] Share note editor and wire account save/reload with account-scoped state.
- [x] Verify two-account handler/database/browser lifecycle with isolated synthetic data, failed writes and reload.
- [x] Full checks, checked push/exact CI, durable docs/receipts. Hosted gates above remain open.

Source `09866165252689297718414a55c3eecee7f5956b`, pushed to origin/main. Shared local/account page-note editor supports create/edit/delete, page anchors and explicit save failure/retry. Real account normalization retains only positive safe-integer page numbers. Account-scoped article query keys and keyed PDF mounts isolate saved content and drafts. No schema change or production dependency was needed.

`pnpm quality` passes 126 app and 20 extension tests, full type/lint/coverage/build/docs/code-health gates. `pnpm test:account-notes` passes two tests using unchanged Hono handlers and Drizzle against isolated SQLite; authentication and PDF bytes are synthetic. It verifies real ownership predicates, sanitization, anchor round trips and invalid anchors, failed PUT/no database change/draft retry, page-two create/reload/navigation/edit/reopen/delete, and Bob independent notes. PUT and GET responses are separately held across a same-SPA Alice-to-Bob Better Auth visibility refresh; late responses never expose Alice content or drafts in Bob's UI. Bob's foreign write returns 404. Guest PDF and account-control browser regressions pass, with independent 390/1440 source/visual review.

Exact [CI](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/reader/actions/runs/34115865848) and [Docs](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/reader/actions/runs/34115865926) passed, including the new real-handler browser suite.

This completes the bounded account page-note implementation. This issue stays open for its original hosted import/annotation/reopen and broader article/extension gates. No hosted upload, provider call, deployment or migration occurred. External browser requests were blocked. The whole-note-array PUT contract does not merge simultaneous editors across tabs/devices; page notes are not text-selection highlights or embedded PDF/export annotations.

## Account article reconciliation repair

Reproduced on `0986616` with the built SPA and real local article handlers: leave an article for `/extension` without unmounting QueryClient, update two notes in isolated SQLite, reopen, edit the stale cached note. The real PUT replaced both current server notes with one stale edited note. Earlier malformed auxiliary-map fixture failures are not product evidence.

Requirements: clean note state SHALL refresh from fetched article notes; reading SHALL not create annotation writes; pending writes SHALL preserve newer edits and be serialized; account/article cache and draft ownership SHALL align. Existing selection/anchor/edit semantics remain. No new schema, dependencies, hosted calls or deployment.

- [x] Repair clean-note reconciliation, dirty-save gating and account-scoped reader state.
- [x] Verify actual selection/create/retry/edit/reload/delete, fresh-cache reopen, pending-edit and account-switch behavior through real handlers/SQLite.

## Account article completion receipt

Source `bec336d2b988b13ed85285aefddc4a36cf788bf4`, pushed to origin/main. The reproduced cached-reopen note loss is repaired: clean notes reconcile with fetched article data, refreshed note IDs remain unique, and reads make no writes. ReaderClient and ReaderCore share account-scoped cache keys; the reader mount is keyed by account/article. Dirty edits are protected from refetch, stale acknowledgements cannot clear newer changes, and marker reanchoring uses the same serialized queue. Failed writes remain failed until explicit retry or a new edit.

`pnpm quality` passes 126 app and 20 extension tests, all existing quality thresholds, builds and docs. The account suite now passes four tests (two PDF, two article), with actual built browser/Hono/Drizzle/isolated SQLite evidence. It covers the same-cache `/extension` reopen regression; selection-menu note creation; failed PUT with no automatic retry, manual retry, reload, edit, delete; fresh GET during a dirty edit; a physical marker drag while a save is held with no extra write; latest text/anchor persistence; and a delayed Alice save crossing a same-SPA Bob session switch. Bob cannot read/write Alice's article and can independently save/reopen his note. Local IndexedDB and guest PDF regressions also pass. The original HTTP 500 was made into a safe expected error value, with sanitized diagnostics and token refunds retained. The guest cover-letter route now resolves local jobs. Its Worker module-load EvalError was fixed by replacing the scraper's module-scope `new Function()` imports.

## Export repair specification

### Why
A guest can generate and save a tailored resume but cannot take that result into a document for an application. The base editor already supports browser Print; preserve that private local-data design.

### What and design
Add one browser-local export control to tailored results and the guest editor. Support Print / Save PDF through a standalone print-ready document, plus downloadable Markdown/plain text, HTML and Word-compatible .doc. Preserve signed-in server export. Share a pure Markdown-to-HTML module with the existing renderer; exclude executable raw HTML, unsafe links, external images and CSS injection. No new dependencies, public rendering endpoint, D1 writes or production configuration.

### Requirements and scenarios
- WHEN a guest exports the current edited or tailored source, THEN the document SHALL contain that source rather than an older server or saved version.
- WHEN Print / Save PDF is selected, THEN a standalone print-ready document SHALL open using the existing templates, with no app navigation in print output. Browser print must allow PDF saving.
- WHEN HTML, text or Word is selected, THEN a correctly named local download SHALL contain the candidate facts and relevant formatting. Word SHALL be labeled .doc, not DOCX.
- WHEN resume input contains script tags, event handlers, dangerous links, external images or malformed render configuration, THEN exported HTML SHALL not execute or fetch those resources.
- WHEN the browser blocks a print window, THEN the UI SHALL explain recovery without discarding source.
- Existing signed-in ownership checks and server exports SHALL remain intact.

## Context

App Health V0 is live at `health.sassmaker.com` / `ingest.sassmaker.com`.
The owner narrative and the Site Health dossier both identify the next
decision as integrating App Health across the owned Fleet production
services and letting observed failures drive future improvements.

Current adoption is uneven:

- `free-ai` already sends full endpoint telemetry via `@saas-maker/app-health/hono`.
- Several projects use the zero-dependency `ping.ts` server log client
  (`high-signal`, `issue-pages`, `anime-list`, `calorie`, `karte`, `live`,
  `on-record`, etc.).
- Many static/landing sites embed the `public/app-health-log.js` browser
  snippet.
- The majority of Fleet projects have no App Health integration yet.

## Goal

Make App Health the default observability layer for endpoint health and
owner-authored logs across all Fleet production services, using official
SDKs/drop-ins, product-scoped ingest keys, and fail-open configuration.

## In scope

- Add endpoint telemetry to every Fleet service that serves HTTP traffic.
- Add owner-authored application logs where useful (sign-ups, payments,
  moderation, webhooks, errors, etc.).
- Provision one App Health app and environment per Fleet project and per
  deployed environment (`local` / `staging` / `production`).
- Configure `APP_HEALTH_INGEST_KEY` and `APP_HEALTH_ENVIRONMENT` per
  deployment.
- Verify each integration reaches "connected" state and populates the
  App Health dashboard.
- Track the rollout in this issue and document the pattern.

## Out of scope

- New App Health product features (alerts, incidents, stored trace
  exploration, teams/roles, billing).
- Removing PostHog, Sentry, or other existing observability tools.
- Changes to the App Health backend architecture.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Inventory** — List every Fleet project that serves production traffic,
   its runtime, and current App Health state.
2. **Choose the official adapter per project** — Express, Hono, Pages,
   Go Echo, Go net/http, OpenTelemetry, or browser log snippet.
3. **Provisioning** — Create an App Health app per project, store
   `APP_HEALTH_INGEST_KEY` as a secret, set `APP_HEALTH_ENVIRONMENT`.
   Services must remain functional when the key is missing (fail-open).
4. **Privacy boundary** — Only method, normalized route, status, duration,
   timestamp, and optional release. Never capture headers, bodies, cookies,
   identity, or stacks.
5. **Verification** — Confirm observed endpoints/logs appear in the
   dashboard for each environment.
6. **Tracking** — This issue is the fleet-wide epic. Each project gets its
   own linked issue/PR.
7. **Documentation** — Add a fleet integration runbook summarizing the
   per-runtime pattern, key management, and environment naming convention.

## Rollout plan

1. **Phase 1 — high-traffic backends**: free-ai, high-signal API,
   issue-pages worker, anime-list worker, karte, live, on-record, calorie.
2. **Phase 2 — static/landing sites with existing browser logs**: verify
   public keys and add endpoint telemetry where backends exist.
3. **Phase 3 — remaining Fleet projects**: integrate any project with no
   current App Health wiring.
4. **Phase 4 — observe and act**: review dashboard health states and file
   follow-up issues for failures that should drive improvements.

## Why

Mashup already has the editorial engine for source-faithful podcast clipping, but its current short lane produces one local clip at a time. The first useful product proof is not a generalized clip factory or a hosted SaaS. It is a local operator desk that can take an entitled archive in one field—starting with **Startups**—and reliably prepare a small, varied batch for human review and posting.

The operator needs to learn whether category-led curation creates repeat value before Mashup grows URL intake, accounts, scheduling, or publishing. The pilot must preserve Mashup's source-rights, provenance, approval, and non-repetition boundaries.

## What

### Phase 0: Startups operator pilot

- Add a checked-in `startups` collection preset with a concise editorial identity and reusable angles such as product-market fit, fundraising, distribution, hiring, founder failure, moats, and contrarian lessons.
- Add a batch-short planning command that generates 3–5 distinct 30–60 second clips for one angle.
- Reject repeated or overlapping source windows across the whole batch.
- Add an explicit vertical social render profile targeting 1080×1920, with source-faithful fit rather than destructive face-blind cropping.
- Burn readable social captions, preserve source heading and collection watermark, and keep the normal EDL score terms and provenance.
- Write a batch manifest and a static local review index linking each clip's preview, transcript/EDL, source, status, and export artifact.
- Keep approval and posting manual. Track review state locally; do not call social platforms.

### In scope

- Local creator-owned, licensed, or public-domain media already acquired by the operator.
- One collection (`startups`) and one operator.
- CLI and machine-agent support for repeatable batch creation.
- Review/download/export artifacts under the requested output directory.
- Focused Python and web/static-output verification.

### Out of scope

- URL, YouTube, or RSS acquisition.
- Hosting, accounts, billing, teams, or multi-tenant storage.
- Social OAuth, scheduling, direct publication, or engagement scraping.
- Face tracking, speaker diarization, auto-reframing, word-level karaoke captions, or synthetic speech.
- Claims about virality or automated rights clearance.
- Production deployment or new paid/provider dependencies.

## Design

The local collection preset supplies the page identity and angle vocabulary. Existing archive ingestion, enrichment, embeddings, and retrieval remain unchanged. Batch planning repeatedly selects complete short windows while excluding source intervals already chosen by the batch. Each selected EDL is rendered with an explicit social profile and recorded in one batch manifest. A generated local review index reads that manifest; it does not introduce a new service or database.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Entitled startup media] --> B[Existing ingest and enrichment]
  P[Startups collection preset] --> C[Batch short planner]
  B --> C
  C --> D[3-5 non-overlapping EDLs]
  D --> E[1080x1920 renders and captions]
  E --> F[Local review index and manifest]
  F --> G[Manual approval and posting]
```

The existing Astro/React transcript editor keeps its visual language. The new review artifact is an operator surface: compact, source-forward, responsive, and honest about local-only state. There is no deployment impact.

## Specs

### Requirement: Collection preset

Mashup SHALL expose a `startups` preset with a stable identifier, display name, watermark, editorial description, and reusable category angles. The operator SHALL be able to override the angle with a free-form prompt.

#### Scenario: Discover startup angles

- **WHEN** the operator lists collections
- **THEN** Mashup reports the Startups preset and its available angles without loading a model or archive

### Requirement: Distinct clip batch

Mashup SHALL create 3–5 complete 30–60 second EDLs from one enriched archive. No two selected clips SHALL repeat a material identifier or overlap planned source audio. Planning SHALL fail clearly when the archive cannot supply the requested count.

#### Scenario: Generate a fundraising batch

- **WHEN** the operator requests five Startups clips for the `fundraising` angle
- **THEN** five ranked EDLs are written with stable indexes and pairwise non-overlapping source ranges

#### Scenario: Insufficient distinct material

- **WHEN** fewer than the requested number of complete, non-overlapping windows exist
- **THEN** no misleading complete batch is reported and the result states the achieved and requested counts

### Requirement: Vertical social rendering

Mashup SHALL accept an explicit social render profile that outputs 1080×1920 H.264 video. Landscape source SHALL be fitted within the frame without face-blind destructive cropping. Captions, source heading, and the Startups watermark SHALL remain readable inside conservative mobile safe areas.

#### Scenario: Render landscape podcast footage

- **WHEN** a landscape source clip is rendered with the social profile
- **THEN** the output is 1080×1920, preserves the full source frame, includes burned captions, and retains source attribution

### Requirement: Local review batch

Mashup SHALL write a versioned JSON batch manifest and a local responsive HTML review index. Each item SHALL expose preview, angle, duration, score, source title/timecode, EDL path, caption path, video path, and review state. The index SHALL not require a running backend.

#### Scenario: Review after rendering

- **WHEN** the batch command completes
- **THEN** the operator can open one local index and play or inspect every generated candidate

### Requirement: Existing boundaries

Every output SHALL retain the eight independent score terms. Rendering SHALL remain approval-compatible, provenance SHALL remain available, and Mashup SHALL not publish media or introduce synthetic speech.

#### Scenario: No external side effect

- **WHEN** a Startups batch is generated and reviewed
- **THEN** no account, social platform, or production service is contacted

## Tasks

- [x] 1. Add collection preset models, Startups content, CLI discovery, and tests.
- [x] 2. Implement distinct batch-short selection and batch manifest validation with focused tests.
- [x] 3. Add explicit 1080×1920 social rendering and safe caption/source treatment with render tests.
- [x] 4. Add the static local review index and responsive operator design evidence.
- [x] 5. Expose the batch through the strict agent manifest with validate-only behavior.
- [x] 6. Document the pilot workflow and update durable project status after verification.
- [x] 7. Run Python tests, Ruff checks, Astro check/build, render smoke tests, and design workflow checks.

## Continue/kill criterion

Run one manually operated Startups page for 20–30 approved clips. Tracking issue for the Look Sideways podcast: recorded conversations with accomplished people about the conditions, sequence, and luck behind their early breakthroughs. Re-files #30, which was closed as not planned pending owner outreach. The owner is now starting the outreach. ## Why Every profile in the archive is reconstructed from third-party sources. The people themselves have never been asked what they brought, what they were handed, what surrounded them, where they persisted, and where a door was encountered rather than authored. A conversation gets at sequence and luck in a way a biography rarely does, and it gives the exhibit a human voice without turning it into a coaching product. The audience is the same as the site's: readers who turn someone else's visible finish into a verdict on themselves. Participants are a second audience: they need to understand the project quickly and trust how their words will be used. ## What In scope: - A participant-facing brief that explains the project and the recording terms (the repository already has `docs/brief.md` as the starting point). - An outreach and scheduling list, kept private, not in this repository. - A consent and retention template covering recording, publication, correction, and takedown. - A recording and transcript workflow. - A way to show what a participant said on their own profile, clearly separated from independently sourced fact. - Decisions about where episodes are hosted and how they are linked from the site. Out of scope: - Any change to the two-independent-source publication gate. Testimony does not admit a person to the archive. - Scores, ratings, or any reading of the interview as evidence for the condition factors. - Editing a participant's account into third-person biography. ## Design Proposed evidence class: `first_person_account`. It is a third layer beside the biographical layer and the annotation layer, never counted toward `minimum_source_origins` or `minimum_independent_sources` in `data/research/coverage/gate-registry.json`, and never used to change a condition-factor score. On a profile it renders as a distinct section, provisionally "In their own words", with a timestamped quote, the episode link, the recording date, and an interpretation boundary stating that this is the participant's account and has not been independently verified. The clarity audit gains a check that the section carries that boundary. Episodes are hosted off-site (YouTube or a podcast host) and linked. The repository stores only the published claims and timestamps, not audio. A `/podcast/` index page lists episodes and links each to the participant's profile where one exists. Participants without a published profile appear on the index only; they do not get a profile through the interview. ```mermaid flowchart LR outreach[Outreach + consent] --> record[Recording] record --> transcript[Transcript] transcript --> claims[Timestamped claims
reviewed by participant] claims --> data[first_person_account
on the record] data --> profile[Profile section
with boundary] data --> index[/podcast/ index] record --> host[Off-site episode host] host --> index ``` ## Specs ### Requirement: testimony is separate from evidence The exhibit SHALL show first-person accounts in a distinct section with an interpretation boundary, and SHALL NOT count them toward any publication gate or score. #### Scenario: participant already has a profile - **WHEN** an episode with a published participant is added - **THEN** their profile shows the account section with quote, timestamp, episode link, date, and boundary, and their condition-factor scores are unchanged #### Scenario: participant has no profile - **WHEN** an episode with a participant who fails the publication gate is added - **THEN** the episode appears on the index with no profile created and no gate bypassed ### Requirement: consent and correction Participants SHALL review the claims drawn from their episode before publication and SHALL be able to request correction or removal. #### Scenario: takedown - **WHEN** a participant requests removal - **THEN** the account section and index entry are removed in the next deploy and the episode link is dropped ### Requirement: participant brief Every participant SHALL receive the same written brief before recording, stating what the project is, what it refuses to do, how their words will be shown, and how to correct or withdraw. ## Tasks - [ ] 1. Define the `first_person_account` fields in the data dictionary and methodology, with the gate-registry note that it is excluded from all gates - [ ] 6. Build the profile section and the `/podcast/` index, including the clarity-audit check for the boundary - [ ] 7. Add the pilot episode's reviewed claims and publish ## Open questions - Which questions form the spine of every episode so accounts are comparable across participants? - Do transcripts get published in full, or only the reviewed claims? - Does the podcast carry the Look Sideways name or a separate one?
